review: Every group in android/gradle/verification-metadata.xml as generated on 2026-10-11 from the tasks in scripts/gradle-verification.mjs (VERIFIED_TASKS) at elizaOS 13c98575987a. The root scripts declare only google(), mavenCentral() and gradlePluginPortal(); included projects also name Maven Central and the plugin portal by URL (scripts/gradle-verification.mjs reads every included build.gradle and fails on anything else); the list is Android (androidx, com.android), Google, JetBrains/Kotlin, Apache, the AndroidX test stack and the transitive libraries of the Android Gradle plugin and lint. No group was unfamiliar. The metadata does not record which of the three repositories served an artifact; the SHA-256 is what is enforced. Engineering review by the round 10 implementer; it is not a security sign-off. In review the 71 shipped coordinates were fetched again from Google's Maven repository (61) and Maven Central (10) and matched the recorded SHA-256. Addition 2026-10-14 at elizaOS 644d56c93d: the pinned plugin-native-reminders declares testImplementation junit 4.13.2 and org.robolectric:robolectric 4.16.1, so lint of :eliza-reminders resolves its unit-test classpath. That added the groups org.robolectric (Robolectric, Google-maintained) and its transitive test-only libraries com.almworks.sqlite4java, com.google.testparameterinjector, com.ibm.icu, org.conscrypt and org.yaml, all from Maven Central. They are unit-test dependencies of a library module and are not packaged in any APK. The SHA-256 values were written by Gradle (--write-verification-metadata sha256 for :eliza-reminders:generateDebugUnitTestLintModel and lintAnalyzeDebugUnitTest) and were not re-fetched independently. The guava-parent 33.4.8-jre POM, which hosted CI resolved but a warm local cache did not, was added from the Gradle-fetched file; its SHA-1 matched the one Maven Central publishes. Addition 2026-10-17: AndroidX Media3 1.11.1 transformer/effect and their transitive Media3 modules are Google-maintained AndroidX artifacts resolved from google(). Their POMs, source API and Apache-2.0 notices were reviewed during native video exporter implementation; Gradle generated SHA-256 pins in strict metadata. Existing groups cover the remaining annotation dependencies. This records engineering review, not an independent security sign-off. Addition 2026-10-25: AndroidX Credential Manager 1.6.0 and Google Identity googleid 1.2.1 provide the native Google account picker; artifacts fetched from official Google Maven and pinned by SHA-256. Native ID tokens remain outside the renderer. Google Play services transitive libraries also independently re-fetched from Google Maven; all 43 new artifact hashes matched. Gradle regenerated metadata preserves pins. Compatibility qualification selects googleid 1.1.1 (Kotlin metadata 1.9) over 1.2.1 (metadata 2.4 unsupported by current lint); both 1.1.1 artifacts independently fetched from official Google Maven and SHA-256 pinned.
